title: Lightweight request-observer adapter for language SDKs
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Problem: SDK customers today see varied integration quality for request-level telemetry: some teams use heavy agents that increase allocations and latency percentile regressions, others ship ad-hoc headers that break context continuity across service boundaries. We need a small, idiomatic adapter for Redwood language SDKs that makes it easy for application code to observe request lifecycle events, propagate a compact correlation context, and emit lightweight trace/metric hooks with minimal overhead.

Goals:
- Provide a minimal 'request-observer' adapter for language SDKs (Node, Python, Go) that exposes lifecycle callbacks (onStart, onChunk, onFinish, onError) and a compliant correlation header format.
- Ensure the adapter is zero-to-low allocations on the hot path and can be turned on per-route or globally via SDK opt-in.
- Support fan-out to multiple backends: OTLP-compatible tracer, internal beaconing (batcher), and console dev-mode logs.
- Maintain backward compatibility with existing tracing propagation headers for customers already using Redwood services.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement full automatic instrumentations for web frameworks. That will be a follow-up integration ticket per framework.
- It does not change runtime routing or routing policy logic in the edge proxy.

Design summary:
- Provide a tiny core interface (single-file in each SDK) implementing the observer pattern. The public API is an immutable RequestContext that carries: trace_id, span_candidate_id, sampling_hint, and an opaque payload map for 3rd-party keys. The adapter exposes a header serializer that produces a compact base64 URL-safe block (<= 80 bytes typical).
- On the hot path (token generation/streaming), we avoid heap allocations by reusing buffers from a sync.Pool (Go), preallocated arrays (Node Buffer pool), and small-object arenas (Python).
- Fan-out is implemented as a set of pluggable sinks behind a single switch: OTLP sink, console sink, and internal-beacon sink. Sinks are registered at SDK init and are no-op if disabled.
- Opt-in modes: "disabled" (default), "dev" (console logs + no export), "standard" (OTLP + beaconing).

Acceptance criteria:
- Adapter implemented in Node/Python/Go SDKs with matching public surface and header serialization.
- End-to-end propagation test across SDK -> edge-proxy -> runtime shows preserved trace_id and consistent sampling hint in 99.99% of test runs.
- Microbenchmark: <1% median latency increase for a 1-token request, and 95th percentile increase <= 3ms on our CI benchmark machines when adapter enabled in "standard" mode.
- Integration tests for fan-out to internal beaconing and to an OTLP collector are green in CI.
- Docs: Confluence design doc + SDK README examples for enabling adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Node/Python/Go adapters implemented and exported in SDKs
Header format documented and compatibility tests added
Performance gate: median <1% and p95 <= 3ms overhead in CI benchmarks
CI integration tests for OTLP and internal-beacon sinks pass
Public README examples and Confluence design doc linked
comments: 2026-02-20 - Amina Patel: Created ticket after spike (notes in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Request+Observer+Adapter). Spike showed feasible low-allocation patterns in Go and Node.

2026-02-25 - Diego Ramirez: Pushed initial PoC for Go: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-sdk/pull/112. PoC uses sync.Pool + fixed-size buffer; microbenchmarks show ~0.6% median overhead, p95 ~2.7ms on c6i-type test machine.

2026-03-01 - Design review (PM+Infra): feedback to keep header <= 96 bytes max and include a single-version byte for forward compatibility. PM (Sofia Li) suggested opt-in flag naming: 'requestObserverMode'.

2026-03-04 - Diego Ramirez: Updated serialization to add version byte and compact map encoding; PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-sdk/pull/129. Also added OTLP sink shim and unit tests.

2026-03-08 - Security review (pre-check): security team requested threat model for header spoofing and recommended HMAC option for high-sensitivity tenants. HMAC addition will be behind 'secure_headers' opt-in (separate follow-up).

2026-03-10 - QA (Jules Chen): Added cross-language propagation test harness. Integration job  observability-propagation-e2e/45 shows 1000/1000 successful propagations for standard sampling rates. Link to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/propagation/observer-e2e

2026-03-12 - Diego Ramirez: Opened RFC-style PR to docs and SDK READMEs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-sdk/pull/141. Next: add Node and Python performance optimizations and prepare release notes for runtime-1.22.
Next steps: finish Node/Python micro-optimizations, add opt-in config surface to console and SDK quickstart, create follow-up ticket for HMAC secure headers (security review required).
